seo_meta_description: Master Systems Of Equations on the Digital SAT using built-in Desmos graphing calculator hacks, syntax commands, regressions, and speed drills.
exam_weightage: Essential Digital SAT Tool (5-8 Questions per Module)

techniques.title: Direct Intersection Finding
techniques.description: Type both equations exactly as they appear. Click the intersection point on the graph to see the (x, y) coordinate.
techniques.when_to_use: Any system with two variables (x, y) where you need the solution point.
techniques.pro_tip: If the intersection is off-screen, click the wrench icon to adjust the axes or zoom out.

techniques.title: Interactive Sliders for Constants
techniques.syntax: y = mx + b, y = ax + c
techniques.description: Use sliders to find values of constants that create specific conditions like 'no solution' (parallel lines) or 'infinitely many' (coincident lines).
techniques.when_to_use: Questions asking for values of constants (k, a, b) that result in specific system behaviors.
techniques.pro_tip: Click the 'play' button on the slider to animate the line and watch the intersection point move.

techniques.title: Substitution via Evaluation
techniques.description: If you find x, type 'x = [number]' into a new line to create a vertical line, then click the intersection with the other equation to find y.
techniques.when_to_use: When you have one variable and need to find the other quickly.
techniques.pro_tip: This is faster than manual substitution and prevents arithmetic errors.

techniques.title: Regression for Systems
techniques.description: Use the tilde (~) to perform linear regression if given a table of values instead of equations.
techniques.when_to_use: Data-based systems questions where you must find the intersection of two trends.
techniques.pro_tip: Ensure you use y1 and x1 to match the table headers.

techniques.title: Inequality Shading Overlap
techniques.description: Graph inequalities and look for the overlapping shaded region.
techniques.when_to_use: Systems of inequalities questions asking if a point (x, y) is a solution.
techniques.pro_tip: Type the point as (x, y) to see if it lands in the dark purple overlapping region.

speed_walkthroughs.problem: The system of equations is $2x + 3y = 12$ and $x - y = 1$. What is the value of $x + y$?

drills.question: Which ordered pair $(x, y)$ is the solution to the system: $y = 2x + 5$ and $y = -x + 2$?
For what value of $k$ does the system $y = 3x + 2$ and $y = 3x + k$ have no solution?
drills.desmos_command: y = 3x + 2, y = 3x + k (add slider for k)
explanation: Adjust k until the lines are parallel and never touch.
Observe that for any k not equal to 2, the lines are parallel.
